findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the MySQL database a publicly resolvable address reachable from outside the VPC in addition to any security group controls, so the database attack surface is exposed to the internet.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage, snapshots and read replicas unencrypted, exposing data if the underlying volume is accessed or snapshotted.

The EC2 user_data script writes the database password (var.password) in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on the instance filesystem; user data is also readable via the instance metadata service and the AWS API, so the credential is disclosed to anything that can reach either.

The DB password (var.password) is interpolated directly into the EC2 user_data startup script, embedding the database credential in the instance's user data, which is retrievable from the instance metadata service and the EC2 API by anyone with access to either.

The policy attached to the catalog app role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the workload full control of S3, EC2 and RDS including the ability to read other buckets, alter security groups and delete or reconfigure databases.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR block rather than scoped to the application tier's security group, so any instance in the VPC can reach the database; combined with publicly_accessible this widens the database's exposure.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing the database to initiate connections anywhere and providing an exfiltration path not needed by a database tier.

The database security group accepts MySQL on 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than from a designated application security group, so access control is not tied to the requesting workload's identity. The exposure is created by the rule resource, and the database also must not be publicly accessible if this rule is the sole control.

The DB subnet group reuses the portal application subnets (aws_subnet.portal_subnet_a/b) that host the public-facing web server rather than dedicated private database subnets, so the database is placed in a network tier that should not carry data-tier resources.

The database master user is set to "admin", the engine's privileged account name, rather than a non-obvious identifier, weakening brute-force and credential-guessing resistance on a database that is also publicly accessible.
